To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the reliability of CT volumetry of lung metastases for the assessment of therapy response depends on the volume change threshold and the number of target metastases; and (2) the reliability of the assessment is highest when at least 3 target lesions are assessed and the threshold for the definition of a response is set to a volume decrease of 35% or more.
the reproducibility for the evaluation of treatment response of pulmonary metastases is robust with a VCT ≥ 35% and a minimum of three target lesions.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach for automated CT volumetry of lung metastases, which has shown to be a reliable method for response assessment in lung metastases under chemotherapy.
the reproducibility and reliability of automated CT-volumetry of pulmonary metastasis for the purpose of response evaluation in clinical trials.
the evaluation of the reproducibility and confidence of CT-volumetry for the assessment of pulmonary metastatic response to therapy using the RECIST criteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CT volumetry of lung metastasis using RECIST is reliable with VCT ≥ 35%.
the number of metastases to be evaluated should be at least 3, and that the volume change threshold should be 35% to obtain a reliable response assessment.
a reduction in target lesions from ≥3 to ≥1 does not significantly affect the reliability of CT-volumetry for treatment response evaluation of pulmonary metastasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a reduced VCT and target lesion number in the RECIST criteria may be a useful approach in the assessment of therapy response for pulmonary metastases.
the reliability of CT volumetry of lung metastasis is very high and that it is possible to shorten the follow-up intervals by decreasing the VCT for response assessment.
a reduction of the volume change threshold for response assessment from 70% (RECIST) to 35% (modified RECIST) is associated with a significant reduction of observer confidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reliability of RECIST criteria in the context of CT volumetry of metastasis is robust for volume change thresholds ≥35%, but decreases with thresholds <35%, and that the reliability of CT volumetry is improved by using ≥3 target metastases.
a VCT of 35% is sufficient for reliable assessment of response to treatment.

a reduction in the VCT to 35% or lower is not recommended in the evaluation of pulmonary metastases with CT volumetry, as it leads to a significant reduction of the reliability of the evaluation of treatment response.
